title: PRD: Enterprise Audit Logs (Schema v1, Export, Retention, Filtering)
author: Naomi Feldman
body:
## Summary
Enterprise customers increasingly require audit logs as a procurement and compliance prerequisite (SOC 2, ISO 27001, internal security monitoring). Today, Redwood emits partial audit events across services with inconsistent naming/fields and limited export options.

This PRD defines enterprise requirements for:
- Canonical audit event schema (v1) + schema stability guarantees
- 100% coverage of “sensitive actions” across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private
- Query + filtering experience (Console + API)
- Export to customer SIEM/log lake (S3 and webhook; Splunk-compatible path)
- Retention, redaction, and reliability (delivery lag SLO) appropriate for audits and incident response

This document is the product contract for Beta and GA readiness.

## Background / Why now
Drivers:
- Multiple enterprise prospects require audit logging completeness + SIEM export prior to security sign-off.
- Private and Dedicated deployments are expanding into regulated workloads; auditability is table stakes.
- Internal security posture: audit logs must be reliable, tamper-resistant, and privacy-aware.

In parallel, Security & Compliance is standardizing the schema and sensitive-action inventory (see related pages). This PRD focuses on customer-facing requirements and acceptance criteria.

## Goals
1) Provide an enterprise-grade audit log product surface area across all deployment modes:
   - Hosted API
   - Dedicated
   - Private (VPC and on-prem)
2) Make audit logs usable for security operations and compliance evidence:
   - Filterable, attributable (who did what), correlated (request_id), and exportable
3) Ensure completeness and reliability:
   - “Sensitive actions” coverage at GA
   - Delivery lag SLO with alerting and documented incident response

## Non-goals (initial GA)
- Full historical backfill for all legacy events (only limited migration/backfill where required by contract)
- Customer-defined custom event schemas (we provide a stable canonical schema)
- Non-sensitive observability events (request/trace logs are separate)
- Long-term data warehouse analytics for audit logs beyond basic query/export

## Personas / Users
- Security Engineer / SOC Analyst: needs SIEM ingestion, reliable timestamps, actor attribution, and high-signal event taxonomy.
- Compliance / GRC: needs evidence of administrative controls and change management.
- Platform Admin (Customer): needs to review “who changed what” in Redwood Console, and export for internal controls.
- Redwood Support / Security (internal): needs restricted access and consistent event debugging paths (governed by policy).

## Definitions
- Sensitive action: an action that materially impacts customer data access, security posture, billing, or availability (canonical inventory maintained by Security & Compliance).
- Audit event: append-only, immutable record of a sensitive action, emitted at execution time with outcome semantics.
- Delivery lag: time from event occurrence (event_time) to event availability for query/export.

## User stories
1) As a customer org admin, I can search audit logs for “API key rotated” and see the actor, time, source IP, and outcome.
2) As a security engineer, I can export audit logs to my S3 bucket (or webhook endpoint) in near-real-time, and verify delivery via metrics and dead-lettering.
3) As a compliance lead, I can demonstrate that privileged actions (RBAC changes, user management, retention changes, deployment rollouts) are consistently logged with a stable schema.
4) As an SRE, I can detect audit log delivery delays/drops, troubleshoot quickly, and meet the delivery SLO.

## Product scope
### In-scope event domains (GA)
- Identity & access
  - User/admin lifecycle: invite, add/remove, deactivate/reactivate
  - SSO/SAML enforcement changes (where applicable)
  - API key creation/rotation/revocation
  - RBAC role and policy bundle changes (including diffs)
- Org/workspace settings
  - Workspace creation/deletion
  - Audit log configuration changes (export sinks, retention tier)
  - Data retention changes for audit logs (and any related retention settings)
- Deployments / availability
  - Model deploy/rollout actions: canary start/stop, pin/unpin versions, fallback policy changes
  - Routing policy changes (cost/latency tier routing)
  - Dedicated capacity scaling and quota changes
  - Private installer actions: install/upgrade/rollback (package version, cluster id)

### Out-of-scope events (Beta)
- Fine-grained “read access” events for every console view (we will capture access to audit logs and certain export actions; not every page view)
- High-volume, low-signal events (e.g., every inference request)

## Requirements
### 1) Schema and stability
- Canonical schema: Audit Event Schema v1 (see related page).
- Versioning:
  - Schema version must be explicit on every event.
  - Backward-compatible additions only within v1 (new optional fields allowed).
  - Breaking changes require v2 and a deprecation window communicated to customers.
- Naming conventions:
  - Event names follow guidelines in “Audit Event Naming Guidelines”.
  - Namespaces must be consistent across systems (e.g., api_key.*, rbac.*, console.*, dedicated.*, private_installer.*) and approved via registry.

Customer-facing commitments:
- GA guarantees:
  - Schema v1 fields required by spec are always present.
  - Event names for GA-sensitive actions are stable (no renames without dual-write + notice period).

### 2) Query and filtering (Console + API)
Functional requirements:
- Console “Audit Logs” page:
  - Filter by: time range, event_name, outcome (success/failure), actor type, actor id/email (if available), resource type/id, workspace/org, source IP, request_id, service.
  - Full-text search across a safe subset (event_name, actor display, target identifiers, request_id) without exposing secrets.
  - Pagination with stable ordering (event_time desc, tie-break by event_id).
- Audit Logs API:
  - Endpoints to list/filter audit events; supports cursor-based pagination.
  - RBAC-enforced access (admin-only by default; roles can be expanded with explicit permission).
  - Rate limiting to protect the pipeline.

Non-functional requirements:
- Query latency target (p95):
  - <= 2.0s for 7-day range with common filters
  - <= 5.0s for 30-day range with filters
- Availability:
  - Audit log query API should meet Console backend SLOs; partial degradation acceptable if export remains functional.

### 3) Export to SIEM / log lake
Must-have sinks for GA:
1) S3 export (primary):
   - Customer-configured bucket + prefix
   - Server-side encryption supported (SSE-S3; SSE-KMS where feasible)
   - Delivery modes:
     - Near-real-time streaming to objects (batched)
     - Periodic rollups (e.g., every 5 minutes) to reduce object count
   - Format:
     - JSON Lines (one event per line)
     - Optionally gzip-compressed objects
   - Partitioning guidance:
     - /org_id=<id>/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hr=HH/…

2) Webhook export:
   - Customer-configured HTTPS endpoint
   - Retries with exponential backoff
   - Signature verification (HMAC) to validate authenticity
   - Dead-letter behavior and replay tooling

Nice-to-have (Beta / early GA):
- Splunk-friendly delivery:
  - Either via webhook (HEC-compatible payload mode) OR documented mapping recipe for Splunk ingestion from S3

Export management requirements:
- Per-org configuration stored and audited (audit events for config changes are required).
- “Test export” action in Console that emits a synthetic event (clearly marked) and verifies sink connectivity.
- Customer can pause/resume exports (action must be audited).

### 4) Retention and redaction
Retention requirements:
- Default retention for Hosted/Dedicated: 30 days (subject to plan).
- Enterprise tiers:
  - 90 days
  - 180 days
  - 365 days
- Private/on-prem:
  - Customer-configurable retention, with recommended defaults and guardrails.

Redaction requirements:
- Audit logs must never include secrets, tokens, raw API keys, or private key material.
- IP and user-agent retention:
  - Must be configurable where required by privacy constraints (e.g., allow truncation/anonymization policy).
  - Default behavior: store IP and user-agent for security monitoring; document purpose and retention.

### 5) Reliability, delivery SLO, and failure semantics
Definitions:
- An event is “delivered” when it is persisted in the canonical store and becomes queryable AND eligible for export.
- Export delivery is sink-specific; pipeline must provide per-sink delivery status metrics.

SLO targets (GA):
- Delivery lag SLO (Hosted/Dedicated):
  - 99.9% of events delivered within 5 minutes
  - 99.99% within 30 minutes
- Export SLO (per sink):
  - 99.9% of events successfully exported within 15 minutes of delivery (excluding customer endpoint downtime)

Required behaviors:
- No sampling (audit logs are not sampled).
- At-least-once delivery to export sinks; events must include stable event_id to allow customer deduplication.
- Backpressure support and dead-letter queues for exporter failures.
- Clear semantics for outcome:
  - success: action completed
  - failure: action failed (include error_code and safe error_message)
  - denied: action blocked by policy/RBAC

Operational requirements:
- Dashboards:
  - enqueue rate, validation failures, persist success rate
  - delivery lag histogram
  - exporter per-sink success/failure, retry queue depth, DLQ growth
- Alerting:
  - Page SRE on sustained lag breach or drop rate above threshold (see telemetry standards).
- Runbook: “Audit Log Delivery Lag Runbook” must be current before GA.

### 6) Security and access control
- Customer access:
  - Audit Logs UI/API is restricted to org admins by default.
  - New permissions for viewing/exporting audit logs must be explicit and audited.
- Internal access:
  - Access to raw audit logs is restricted per policy and must itself be logged.
- Tamper resistance:
  - Append-only storage properties and integrity controls documented (threat model page).

## Feature requirements by deployment mode
### Hosted API
- Full schema v1 for all in-scope sensitive actions.
- Console query + API query.
- S3 + webhook export.

### Dedicated
- Same as Hosted plus dedicated-specific events:
  - capacity scaling/quota changes and initiator (auto/manual)

### Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Must emit schema v1 events locally.
- Export options:
  - On-prem: customer-managed sink; Redwood provides exporter configuration and health status.
  - VPC: S3/webhook supported depending on network egress policy.
- Operator identity captured for installer actions (cluster id, operator, package version).

## Success metrics
Product outcomes:
- Enterprise security review pass rate improves:
  - Reduce “audit logging” as a top-3 blocker in security questionnaires.
- Adoption:
  - % of enterprise orgs enabling export within 30 days of availability.

Engineering outcomes (GA):
- Coverage:
  - 100% of inventory-listed sensitive actions mapped to >= 1 schema-v1 audit event.
  - CI gate prevents new sensitive actions from shipping without a registered event.
- Reliability:
  - Meet delivery lag SLO for 30 consecutive days.
- Supportability:
  - < 2 customer escalations per quarter for missing audit events (post-GA) for covered actions.

## Beta plan
### Beta entry criteria (start Beta)
- Schema v1 published and implemented in shared libraries.
- Console query experience available behind feature flag.
- Export: S3 and webhook available in at least one region/environment.
- Instrumentation for top enterprise-sensitive actions complete:
  - API key create/rotate/revoke
  - RBAC role/policy changes
  - Audit log configuration changes

### Beta cohort
- 3–5 enterprise design partners (mix of Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
- Preference for customers with active SIEM/log lake workflows and clear procurement requirements.

### Beta evaluation rubric
- Completeness: customers can validate required event set for their key controls.
- Usability: filtering/query supports common investigations.
- Export performance: stability under real ingestion rates; retry behaviors acceptable.
- Schema clarity: minimal ambiguity about actor vs target; consistent naming.

### Beta duration
- Target: 4–6 weeks with weekly check-ins.

### Beta exit criteria (ready for GA)
- No P0 issues open related to data loss, schema correctness, or export reliability.
- Delivery lag SLO met for Beta environments.
- Documentation complete:
  - FAQ, schema docs, export setup guides, and runbooks.

## GA acceptance criteria
GA is achieved when all items below are true:

1) Coverage and schema
- Sensitive action inventory shows 100% coverage for GA scope.
- Registry/validator in CI blocks unregistered event names.
- Dual-write and migration plan executed for legacy events where needed for customers.

2) Customer experience
- Console “Audit Logs” page available to enterprise plans (or add-on), with required filters and pagination.
- Audit Logs API is publicly documented for enterprise customers.

3) Export
- S3 export GA (JSONL, gzip optional) with documented IAM/KMS guidance.
- Webhook export GA with HMAC signing, retries, and DLQ.
- “Test export” function and clear health/status indicators.

4) Reliability and operations
- Delivery lag SLO defined, dashboards live, paging policy agreed.
- Runbook validated via at least one game day.

5) Security/compliance readiness
- Redaction rules validated (tests) and documented.
- Access policy for internal audit log access is published and enforced.
- SOC 2 evidence mapping published (for internal audit support).

## Dependencies
- Audit Event Schema v1 publication and shared library rollout (Security/Platform).
- Audit log pipeline capacity and exporter hardening (Telemetry/SRE).
- RBAC permission updates for audit log viewing/exporting (Identity/RBAC team).
- Private installer instrumentation and identity attribution (Private Deployments).

## Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Missing coverage due to fragmented ownership across services.
  - Mitigation: single inventory + CI enforcement + integration tests per sensitive action.
- Risk: PII leakage (IP/user-agent) concerns in certain jurisdictions.
  - Mitigation: configurable retention/anonymization + documented defaults; legal/privacy review.
- Risk: Export reliability blamed on Redwood when customer endpoint is down.
  - Mitigation: clear status signals (customer endpoint unreachable vs Redwood failure), DLQ + replay.
- Risk: High event volume from certain actions (e.g., automated scaling).
  - Mitigation: ensure event taxonomy is meaningful; rate-limit automated actions or aggregate where appropriate (without losing auditability).

## Open questions
1) Splunk: do we ship native HEC mode at GA, or provide a documented recipe from S3/webhook for v1?
2) Retention packaging: which tiers are base enterprise vs compliance add-on?
3) Private/on-prem: what is the minimum exporter footprint and supported sinks for air-gapped environments?
4) IP/user-agent: what exact configuration options are required (truncate, hash, omit) and per-plan defaults?

## Milestones (target)
- Schema v1 + libraries: complete
- Console query + API: Beta ready
- Exporter hardening + SLO dashboards: Beta mid-point
- Coverage + CI enforcement + integration tests: GA gate

For detailed execution, see Linear initiative “Audit log schema standardization + coverage.”
